title: Siding Software: 9 Tools for Siding Contractors
html:
Siding software pays off when it ties your ad spend to booked jobs. A siding contractor needs a job app, an estimate tool, a photo tool and a way to track which clicks and calls become sales. Pair them with Google Ads management and a siding marketing plan. Published prices below run from free to $299 a month.

Siding software has to do four jobs: find the lead, price the job, track the source and get paid. Siding is a high-ticket trade, so one lost lead costs real money and one untracked ad click wastes it. This guide groups nine tools by the job each one does, with the vendor's own published price and one real limit.

A siding job often runs into five figures, and homeowners get several quotes. Ads bring them in fast, but only if you can see which keywords produce booked estimates.

What does each siding software tool do and cost?

The table lists all nine tools by job, with the entry price each vendor shows. Use it to shortlist, then read the details below.

ToolJob it doesEntry price shown by the vendorMain limit
Google Keyword PlannerKeyword researchNo price stated on the help pageNeeds a finished Google Ads setup
Google Ads conversion trackingCounts calls and formsNo separate price statedImport data takes 24 to 48 hours
CallRailCall tracking$50 a month250 local minutes included
JoistEstimates and invoices$10 a month billed monthly5 documents a month on Basics
JobberScheduling and invoices$49 a month, no commitmentExtra users cost $29 a month
Housecall ProScheduling and invoices$59 a month billed annuallyAdd-ons have no listed price
CompanyCamJob photos$63 a month billed annually2-user limit on Core
Google Business ProfileMap listingFreeNeeds verification and upkeep
Google Ads accountRuns the adsNo sign-up fee statedA small prepayment may be requested

Entry prices read from each vendor page in November 2026. Check the vendor for current plans.

Which siding software shows whether your Google Ads work?

Google Keyword Planner, Google Ads conversion tracking and CallRail answer the first question every siding advertiser has: which clicks become jobs.

  • Google Keyword Planner: suggests keywords and gives forecasts inside Google Ads. Limit: you must finish Google Ads account setup, including billing details, before you can use it, and forecasts are estimates, not guarantees.
  • Google Ads conversion tracking: counts calls, form fills and other actions using the Google tag, Google Analytics key events or Google Tag Manager. Limit: imported options can take 24 to 48 hours to appear, and running a plugin plus a manual tag can double-count.
  • CallRail: call tracking numbers that show which ad or page produced each call. Lead Tracking is $50 a month with 250 local minutes and 5 local numbers. Limit: usage beyond the plan is billed extra, with local minutes at $0.05 each.

Siding buyers often call after a long research phase, so many leads arrive by phone. A form-only setup misses them. Track calls and forms in the same account so cost per booked estimate comes from one report.

Set the keywords by job type. Siding replacement, vinyl, fiber cement and storm repair behave differently, and they need separate campaigns.

Which siding contractor software handles estimates and invoices?

Joist is an estimate and invoice app, which makes it a light choice for a small siding crew that does not need dispatch.

  • Joist: sends estimates and invoices and takes online payments. Basics is $10 a month billed monthly, and Pro is $17 a month billed monthly. Limit: Basics allows up to 5 documents a month, so a busy crew outgrows it quickly.

A siding quote depends on square footage, product, trim, house height and removal of old siding. Keep one template per product line. The faster a quote goes out after the walk-around, the better its chance against the other two or three bids.

Which siding software runs jobs and crews?

Jobber and Housecall Pro are the two job apps that siding contractors compare first. Both handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments.

  • Jobber: covers scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. The Core plan for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Limit: each extra user costs $29 a month, and Marketing Suite at $99 a month is billed on top.
  • Housecall Pro: covers scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments. Basic is $59 a month billed annually for one user, and Essentials is $149 a month billed annually for five users. Limit: the page lists several add-ons without prices.

Both vendors charge card processing fees. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents for credit cards and 1% for bank payments, and Housecall Pro says its card rates start at 2.59%. On a five-figure siding deposit, that fee is large, so ask whether the customer can pay by bank transfer.

Which siding software tracks job photos?

CompanyCam keeps dated photos tied to each job, which suits a trade where the finished wall is the proof.

  • CompanyCam: photo capture with project folders. Core is $63 a month billed annually and includes one user, with a 2-user limit. Limit: extra users cost $29 each, and Core caps video at 5 minutes.

Before and after photos serve two purposes. They settle disputes about existing damage, and they make strong proof for your site.

Which free tool puts a siding company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows a siding company in Google Maps. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, photos, reviews and phone number when homeowners search nearby. Limit: your address must meet Google's guidelines and you must verify the business, and a thin listing rarely stands out.

What numbers should siding software track?

Siding software should track five numbers: cost per click, calls, booked estimates, win rate and revenue per job. Together they show whether ad spend becomes jobs.

  • Cost per booked estimate: divide ad spend by estimates that reach the walk-around. This number matters more than cost per click.
  • Win rate: divide signed jobs by estimates delivered. A low rate points to quote speed or price, not ad quality.
  • Revenue per job: compare full replacements with repairs. A repair lead is worth less, so bid on it differently.
  • Call answer rate: count missed calls by hour. Missed calls during crew hours are the cheapest leak to fix.

Most apps hold the first four numbers if you enter the lead source on every job. Add one required field for source and review the report monthly.

How should a siding company set up its first 30 days of software?

Set up tracking before you raise ad spend, then add the office tools one week at a time. A crew adopts one new habit at a time.

  • Week 1: set up conversion tracking and a call tracking number, then test both with a real call and a real form.
  • Week 2: choose an estimate app, build quote templates per product and send the next quote from it.
  • Week 3: add before and after photos to every job folder, named by address.
  • Week 4: review cost per booked estimate and decide whether a full job app earns its monthly price.

What software mistakes cost siding companies the most?

The costliest siding software mistake is paying for ad clicks without tracking the call or form that follows. The other common mistakes are smaller, but they add up.

  • Tracking only forms: siding buyers call, so a form-only report undercounts leads and makes good keywords look weak.
  • Buying seats early: every extra user on Jobber costs $29 a month, so add seats when a second crew actually starts.
  • Skipping templates: without a template per product, each quote is built from scratch and goes out days late.
  • Ignoring card fees: processing fees on a large deposit can exceed the monthly plan price, so compare payment options.
  • No photo habit: when photos are optional, they stop, and the proof for disputes and for your site is gone.

How can you test a siding software tool before you pay?

Test a tool by running one real job through it end to end. Jobber, Housecall Pro and CallRail each list a 14-day free trial on their plans, so read the trial terms first.

  • Pick a real lead: use a live estimate, not demo data, so you see the real steps.
  • Time each step: record minutes to build the quote, send it and take the deposit.
  • Check the export: confirm you can pull customer and job data out if you leave.
  • Read the cancel terms: annual plans are cheaper per month but can be non-refundable, as Jobber states for annual payments.

How do you choose siding software?

Choose siding software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: can it quote by product line and square foot, attach photos, and record the lead source?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users, call minutes and card processing fees, then compare the total with one average siding job.

Setup effort: can one person load templates and customers in a weekend, or does it need training and an onboarding fee?

Shop sizeStarter stackPublished price from the vendors above
Owner and one crewJoist Basics, CallRail Lead Tracking, Business Profile$10 a month billed monthly, plus $50 a month
Two or three crewsJobber Core, CompanyCam Core, CallRail Lead Tracking$49 a month, $63 billed annually, $50 a month
Multi-crew shopHousecall Pro Essentials, CompanyCam, CallRail Lead Tracking Complete$149 a month billed annually, plus $63 billed annually and $95 a month

Example stacks built from the plan prices above, read from each vendor in November 2026. Taxes, extra users and usage fees are not included.

What software does a siding contractor need?

A siding contractor needs a way to quote jobs, schedule crews, track lead sources and collect payment. It also needs a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find the company. Start with call and conversion tracking, then add an estimate app, then a job app once several crews run at once.

How much does siding software cost?

Plans here run from free, for Business Profile, to $299 a month for the top Housecall Pro plan. That price is billed annually. Joist Basics costs $10 a month billed monthly, and CallRail starts at $50 a month. Card fees, extra users and usage cost more, so check each vendor.

Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a siding company?

Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually. Run the free trial each vendor offers before you commit.

What software tracks Google Ads leads for siding companies?

Google Ads conversion tracking counts calls and forms using the Google tag, Google Analytics key events or Google Tag Manager. A call tracking tool such as CallRail adds the source of each phone call. Test both with a real call before you raise your ad budget.

Do siding companies need a website if they use job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A site with a page for each siding product and a quote form gives homeowners a reason to call you. It also gives ads a place to send clicks.

Is Google Business Profile free for a siding company?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: verification, accurate service areas, photos of finished walls and replies to every review. Google ad products are separate and are billed on their own terms.

What should a new siding company buy first?

Set up conversion tracking, call tracking and a free Google Business Profile first. Then add an estimate and invoice app such as Joist. Move to full job management only when scheduling several crews becomes the bottleneck, because seats and add-ons raise the price quickly.

-
Ignoring card fees:
processing fees on a large deposit can exceed the monthly plan price, so compare payment options.
-
No photo habit:
when photos are optional, they stop, and the proof for disputes and for your site is gone.
##
How can you test a siding software tool before you pay?
Test a tool by running one real job through it end to end. Jobber, Housecall Pro and CallRail each list a 14-day free trial on their plans, so read the trial terms first.
-
Pick a real lead:
use a live estimate, not demo data, so you see the real steps.
-
Time each step:
record minutes to build the quote, send it and take the deposit.
-
Check the export:
confirm you can pull customer and job data out if you leave.
-
Read the cancel terms:
annual plans are cheaper per month but can be non-refundable, as Jobber states for annual payments.

How do you choose siding software?
Choose siding software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.
Fit:
can it quote by product line and square foot, attach photos, and record the lead source?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra users, call minutes and card processing fees, then compare the total with one average siding job.
Setup effort:
can one person load templates and customers in a weekend, or does it need training and an onboarding fee?

###
What software does a siding contractor need?
A siding contractor needs a way to quote jobs, schedule crews, track lead sources and collect payment. It also needs a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find the company. Start with call and conversion tracking, then add an estimate app, then a job app once several crews run at once.
###
How much does siding software cost?
Plans here run from free, for Business Profile, to $299 a month for the top Housecall Pro plan. That price is billed annually. Joist Basics costs $10 a month billed monthly, and CallRail starts at $50 a month. Card fees, extra users and usage cost more, so check each vendor.
###
Is Jobber or Housecall Pro better for a siding company?
Both cover scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Jobber lists a one-user plan at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists one user at $59 a month billed annually. Run the free trial each vendor offers before you commit.
###
What software tracks Google Ads leads for siding companies?
Google Ads conversion tracking counts calls and forms using the Google tag, Google Analytics key events or Google Tag Manager. A call tracking tool such as CallRail adds the source of each phone call. Test both with a real call before you raise your ad budget.
###
Do siding companies need a website if they use job software?
Yes. Job software runs the work after a lead arrives, but it does not bring leads in. A site with a page for each siding product and a quote form gives homeowners a reason to call you. It also gives ads a place to send clicks.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for a siding company?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: verification, accurate service areas, photos of finished walls and replies to every review. Google ad products are separate and are billed on their own terms.
###
What should a new siding company buy first?
Set up conversion tracking, call tracking and a free Google Business Profile first. Then add an estimate and invoice app such as Joist. Move to full job management only when scheduling several crews becomes the bottleneck, because seats and add-ons raise the price quickly.
